thesis: AES was essentially flat at $15.01 (from $14.97) on 10.9x volume, one cent above the $15.00-per-share cash price in its take-private by a consortium led by Global Infrastructure Partners (BlackRock) and EQT. On Nov 17 the company received final FERC approval, the last suspensory regulatory approval, and expects the deal to close on Dec 2, 2026; shareholders approved it with about 97.9% of votes cast, and the last NYSE trading day is expected to be Dec 1. The volume reflects merger-arbitrage and delisting mechanics, not new operating information. The litigation check found plaintiff-firm fiduciary-duty investigations (Johnson Fistel, Ademi, Halper Sadeh, Kaskela) and two disclosure suits over the proxy, which the company answered with supplemental disclosures, plus a separate Sinolam anticompetition suit in Panama; no scheduled ruling found and no restatement. Upside is capped at the deal price, so the move is mechanical; low, avoid.
invalidation: The merger is terminated or its terms change before the Dec 2 closing, so the stock trades on fundamentals again.

thesis: Brookfield Infrastructure Corp rose about 4.1% to $41.84 (from $40.18) on 5.5x volume; this run found no company news dated today. The stock is in the final days of Brookfield Infrastructure's corporate simplification: the company said on Nov 5 that all required approvals were received, the simplification is expected to close on Nov 19, 2026, and the new shares are expected to begin trading on the NYSE and TSX under the symbol BIP on or about Nov 23. The company also said it is not declaring a fourth-quarter 2026 distribution at this time. Today's volume and the 60-day move reflect exchange and index mechanics around the simplification rather than a new operating result (the Q3 report was on Nov 6). The litigation check found no lawsuit, investigation or restatement tied to the simplification. A mechanical, structure-driven move makes this low; avoid.
invalidation: The simplification closes and the combined BIP shares trade on a company-disclosed result or a declared distribution.

thesis: Global-e fell about 4.6% to $37.99 (from $39.81) on 5.2x volume after its Nov 18 Q3 report, having been down roughly 12-14% premarket. Revenue rose 42% to $314.1M, above the ~$312.9M estimate, and coverage says the outlook was raised; but the adjusted gross margin narrowed to 44.8% from 46.3%, and analysts also pointed to early-November share sales by the president and CEO. The litigation check found no lawsuit or investigation; a March 2026 6-K corrected a scrivener's error in the 2025 20-F about merchant-base GMV share, which is not a restatement of financial results. A revenue beat and raised outlook offset by margin compression and insider selling makes the evidence mixed; low, avoid.
invalidation: Margins re-expand in the next report and the shares recover above the pre-report close (~$39.81).

thesis: Primo Brands fell about 5.4% to $22.935 (from $24.25) on 4.6x volume after gapping down at the open; this run found no company announcement explaining the move, and one report ties it to modest weakness in beverage peers on a day the Russell 2000 fell about 1.5%. thesis: Wolverine World Wide rose about 4.9% to $25.87 (from $24.67) on 3.5x volume, touching a new 52-week high of $25.98, and is up about 27% over 60 days. The company-specific catalyst is its Q3 2026 report (quarter ended Oct 3, filed with the SEC around Nov 12): revenue rose to $505.4M from $470.3M, Saucony grew 19.4% to $158.9M, Merrell grew 6.5% to $178.2M, and the company raised its 2026 outlook to revenue of $2.0-2.01B and adjusted EPS of $1.95-1.99. Counter-cases remain open: the quarter included a non-recurring $35.3M IEEPA tariff refund that the prior outlook excluded, sources disagree on the EPS range (one cites $1.88-1.92), the CEO sold about $1.83M of stock around Nov 16, and adjusted results exclude legal-settlement and environmental costs tied to legacy PFAS exposure (no scheduled ruling found this run). This run found no company news dated today. The litigation check found no restatement. A confirmed beat-and-raise with the one-off tariff refund unresolved makes this medium.
invalidation: Revenue growth stalls, the raised outlook is cut, PFAS costs rise materially, or a close back below ~$22.87 (the Nov 12 close, before the post-report move).

thesis: SELLAS fell about 6.3% to $17.945 (from $19.15) on 2.8x volume, one day after the stock rose about 156% from $7.47 when its Phase 3 REGAL trial of galinpepimut-S in acute myeloid leukemia met its primary overall-survival endpoint: a 41% reduction in the risk of death (HR 0.59, two-sided p=0.035; median OS 24.0 vs 14.7 months). After the close on Nov 17 the company announced a $150M underwritten public offering of common stock with a 30-day option for $22.5M more, which is what today's decline reflects. The company plans to meet the FDA while preparing a BLA. Counter-cases remain open: the offering dilutes holders, the p-value is modest, and at least one prominent commentator has questioned the data; this run found no company press release or wire report, only secondary coverage. The litigation check found no lawsuit, investigation or restatement. A confirmed pivotal-trial win paired with a large equity raise carries a dilution risk flag, which makes this low.
invalidation: FDA feedback questions the overall-survival result or the BLA timeline slips, or the shares give back the post-data move (a close back below the $7.47 pre-data close).
sources: Yahoo Finance (stock soars on positive cancer trial): https://finance.yahoo.com/healthcare/articles/sellas-life-sciences-stock-soars-141221879.html

thesis: BETA Technologies fell about 2.6% to $20.045 (from $20.59) on 3.0x volume, after trading down as much as about 9% intraday, extending a slide from $28.09 on Nov 10. Investing.com ties the drop to a short report from Gotham City Research that values the stock at no more than $10 per share; MarketBeat also points to insider sales, including about 280,000 shares sold by the CTO on Nov 13 at about $23.78 and 15,000 shares by CEO Kyle Clark on Nov 16. The litigation check found a Schall Law investigation announced in April 2026 (no filed complaint found) and a board-initiated independent review after an executive appeared in DOJ-released Epstein-matter materials; no restatement or scheduled ruling found. A short-report and insider-selling-driven move with no company-disclosed result makes this low; avoid.
invalidation: The company answers the short report with disclosed results or contracts and the shares stabilize.

thesis: ZIM rose about 0.7% to $29.91 (from $29.69) on 3.1x volume after its Nov 18 Q3 report (6-K): revenue rose 53% to about $2.71B, net income was about $830M ($6.88 diluted EPS) versus $123M a year earlier, the average freight rate rose 55% to $2,480 per TEU on 4% volume growth, 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised to $3.3-3.5B, and a $2.01 dividend is payable Dec 8. The muted reaction reflects what dominates the share price: an agreed takeover by Hapag-Lloyd (reported at $35 per share) that trade press describes as in limbo, with a rival $4.5B bid, a full Brazilian antitrust review that could run to March 2027, Israeli national-security concerns, and a proxy contest. The earnings are also driven by freight rates, which are cyclical. The litigation check found no lawsuit and no restatement; the deal reviews are regulatory, not litigation. A strong beat offset by an unresolved takeover process that anchors the price makes the evidence mixed; low, avoid.
invalidation: The takeover is completed, abandoned or repriced, so the shares trade on fundamentals again.

thesis: H World fell about 2.3% to $52.44 (from $53.65) on 2.7x volume, its second day giving back part of Monday's post-report gain, but it remains above the ~$50.39 pre-report close and about 7.4% below its 52-week high. A confirmed beat-and-raise with same-hotel RevPAR still declining makes this medium.
invalidation: Same-hotel RevPAR declines deepen, the raised guidance is cut, or a close back below the pre-report close (~$50.39).

thesis: Viking rose about 6.5% to $100.365 (from $94.28) on 2.3x volume, a second day of gains after its Nov 17 Q3 report, which missed on both lines: adjusted EPS of $1.11 against a $1.27 estimate and revenue of $2.184B (up 9.2%) below estimates, with low European river levels costing about $100M of revenue and margin. The rally is attributed to analyst actions (Morgan Stanley raised its target to $100, Barclays to $111, Wells Fargo raised on ROIC strength, while JPMorgan cut to $122 from $131) and to the view that the miss was weather-driven; the company also repurchased $350M of stock in the quarter and held $4.1B of cash. Sell-side targets following the stock do not resolve the miss. The litigation check found no 2026 lawsuit or investigation, only older matters (the 2019 Viking Sky class action and an insurance suit). A miss with the rebound resting on analyst opinion makes the evidence mixed; low, avoid.
invalidation: A company disclosure shows river disruptions do not recur and next-quarter results return to beating estimates.

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 28 on the Oct 27 proposal). Centene fell about 7.1% to $67.42 (from $72.55), closing below the ~$68.03 pre-report level that the prior thesis named as its invalidation point. The drop was part of a second day of selling across managed care after Medicare on Monday (Nov 16) proposed wider use of audit results: Humana fell about 13%, UnitedHealth about 10% and Elevance about 7.6% at the close, and analysts flagged the audit framework as a sector-wide negative. This is a sector-wide regulatory shock rather than company news, but it adds Medicare audit exposure to the counter-cases the prior thesis already named (roughly $0.50 of non-recurring 2026 EPS, Medicaid membership declines and margin pressure, the Arkansas and Hawaii Medicaid exits, the $448M star-ratings dispute, and the Lunstrum class action). The Oct 27 Q3 beat and raised guidance (at least $5.20 of 2026 adjusted EPS) no longer support holding once the price has broken the level the thesis set. The position opened well outside the early-exit window, so the exit is not guarded.
invalidation: A close back above the ~$68.03 pre-report level with CMS narrowing or withdrawing the audit proposal.
sources: EarningsWhispers (Q3 2026 results and guidance, prior thesis source): https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/CNC/202609

thesis: Held position (opened Nov 3 on the Nov 2 proposal; trimmed toward its low-conviction target on Nov 9). invalidation: Q4 results miss the guide or the cash-flow outlook is cut again, a further impairment, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$5.08).
